title: Assessing the role of corticostriatal circuitry in polysubstance use of fentanyl and methamphetamine using rat self-administration models
text:
Polysubstance use of fentanyl and methamphetamine is increasingly common and associated with substantial
morbidity and mortality, yet vastly understudied. The proposed research will use animal models of polysubstance
use that mimic patterns of drug use in humans to examine the striatal neural mechanisms that underlie addiction-
related behaviors. This work is significant as it will let us identify what neural cells and adaptations may be
particularly relevant targets for therapies aimed at addressing polysubstance use and addiction.

title: Peaks to genes: Fine mapping of QTLs and functional analysis
text:
Core B will conduct molecular and bioinformatic analyses of cross progeny to determine the location
of QTLs. As each QTL may contain multiple genes, we will use a suite of methods to fine map QTLs,
followed by CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing to determine the causative genes and SNPs within each QTL
region. This Core will work closely with RP01, RP02 and RP03.

title: Antibody-guided design of a human astrovirus vaccine
text:
Viral diarrheal diseases cause significant suffering worldwide, particularly among children, and human
astrovirus (HAstV) infection is a leading cause of acute viral gastroenteritis. There are over 50 million cases
of HAstV infection globally each year, but despite its clear effect on global public health, no HAstV-specific
vaccines or treatments are available. Together with an extraordinary team of collaborators, we will perform
an ultra-deep survey of the human antibody response to HAstV infection and use this trove of information
to design and test a HAstV vaccine that reliably induces broad, protective immunity.

title: Immunogenomics and Data Core
text: PROJECT SUMMARY – CORE B Next-generation sequencing (NGS) has transformed biological sciences with its high-throughput, scalability, and speed, allowing unprecedented study of biological systems. NGS is now a staple in nearly all biological research fields, particularly in immunology, where the main tissues of interest—immune cells—are more accessible compared to other disciplines. The overarching goal of the Immunogenomics and Data Core (IDC, CORE B) is to provide a suite of sequencing and analysis tools and expertise to support the studies proposed in Projects 1, 2 and 3. Specifically, we will provide the PPG team access to a number of pre-validated genomic assays to study the transcriptome and epigenome of human hematopoietic stem cells and their myeloid and lymphoid counterparts. In addition, we will provide centralized biostatistics and bioinformatics support to the PPG, which will not only advance the research findings but will also facilitate downstream data integration and sharing among all team members, and efficient sharing of such data with others in the field. In addition to providing the analytical solutions needed to address the biological questions described in Projects 1 to 3, the core will establish metrics to ensure that all the data meet high quality-control standards, as well as provide tools to promote data harmonization, security, storage, and maintenance. Ultimately, Core B will enhance the integration of data sets across multiple Projects, facilitating the testing of hypotheses that might not be feasible within the confines of any single Project.

title: Molecular Biology and Genetics: Signaling, Epigenetics and Genome Maintenance
text:
The overall goal of this predoctoral T32 Program under renewal is to offer exceptional interdisciplinary training
in Molecular and Cellular Biology and Genetics with a concentration in cell signaling, epigenetics, and genome
maintenance. There is a critical need for PhD and MD/PhD graduates with extensive training in these areas to
lead development of novel approaches improve outcomes in human conditions in which these processes are
deregulated, including cancer and aging. Our T32 Program aims to meet this need, at the basic science level
and in ways that are relevant to human disease, by our Trainees participating in a set of targeted and evidence-
based activities that will allow them to develop the technical, operational, and professional skills required to
effectively address the nation’s biomedical research agenda.

title: University of Arizona Cancer Center - Cancer Center Support Grant
text:
The mission of the University of Arizona Cancer Center is to alleviate the burden of cancer on patients and families
through scientific collaboration and translation; training and education; and bidirectional communication and
interaction with the communities of our catchment and beyond.

title: HERCULES: Exposome Research Center
text: HERCULES: ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH DATA SCIENCE CORE – SUMMARY Partnering with HERCULES Cores that define and apply (Community Engagement Core, CEC), innovate (Pilot Project Program, PPP), operationalize (Integrated Health Sciences Facility Core (IHSFC), and coordinate and evaluate (Administrative Core), the Environmental Health Data Sciences Core (EHDSC) functions to enable and interpret translational research on the exposome. Specifically, the EHDSC will: 1) Develop and support data pipelines linking the wide range of HERCULES Members’ datasets to projects large and small (Aim 1); 2) Advance expanded and customized data management and analysis plans, implement novel analytic approaches, and expand the HERCULES data and analytic infrastructure (Aim 2); and 3) Provide in-depth introductions and training sessions for HERCULES Members and partners focusing on data science principles, statistical and machine learning design and analysis, and analytic modeling tools of computational systems biology (Aim 3). All three functions are essential to translate exposome-related data of different measurement types taken from different places at different times into informative, interpretable, and communicable results for community members, stakeholders, researchers, and policy makers. Building on a connected collaborative network between our experienced data science professionals and HERCULES Members and community partners, the EHDSC will 1) provide the Administrative Core with insight into existing and emerging trends in data management and analysis from inside and outside the HERCULES community in order to assure training of all Members and support for new and early career investigators; 2) collaborate directly with the CEC in working with HERCULES community partners to identify relevant existing data sources, partnerships with HERCULES Members, and/or support citizen science efforts to provide data collection, data management, and data communication plans; 3) partner with the IHFSC to link health outcomes and exposure measurements in innovative ways quantifying, operationalizing, and interpreting exposome data within translational environmental health research; 4) accelerate the innovative research of the Pilot Program by providing needed support across a range of data science needs. Taken together, the EHDSC provides clear connections to all elements of HERCULES and complements the Administrative Core, the CEC, the Pilot Program, and the IHSFC through close collaboration in our overall mission of learning how the exposome affects health and community well-being and using that knowledge to improve human health.

title: Shared Resource 08:Genomics Shared Resource (GSR)
text: PROJECT SUMMARY – GENOMICS SHARED RESOURCE (GSR) The mission of the Ohio State University Comprehensive Cancer Center Genomics Shared Resource (GSR) is to support OSUCCC members and high-impact cancer research projects with genomics expertise, instrumentation, and centralized resources to generate high-quality data. The GSR is a state-of-the-art genomics laboratory that has substantially increased single-cell sequencing and spatial transcriptomics offerings to meet OSUCCC member needs. The GSR has the following Specific Aims: 1) Generate a broad range of custom and established next-generation sequencing (NGS) library generation types as well as traditional Sanger sequencing and cell-line verification; 2) Offer cutting-edge technology, such as single-cell sequencing and spatial transcriptomics. DNA and RNA isolation from tissues, cells, FFPE samples, and extra-cellular vesicles are supported; and 3) Provide a variety of quantitative gene expression technologies and copy number analysis technologies including NanoString counter, traditional Affymetrix microarrays, digital droplet-PCR, and quantitative real-time PCR-based methods to detect, quantify, and confirm copy number variants, single nucleotide variants, and small insertion/deletion polymorphisms. High-throughput and low-input digital PCR for expression, genotyping, and copy number analyses are also available. Over the current funding cycle, the GSR outsourced NGS sequencing which enabled us to focus more on standard and custom library preparation, avoid the need for replacement of rapidly evolving costly sequencing instruments, and provide competitive pricing. In addition, the OSUCCC invested in new instrumentation for expansion of single-cell and spatial transcriptomics 10X technology. The GSR provided essential genomics expertise and instrumentation to members of all five Research Programs. The GSR has been highly responsive to changing technology and user needs. As a result of user feedback and with OSUCCC and institutional support, the GSR now offers spatial transcriptomics (both 10X Genomics Visium using CytAssist and Bruker GeoMx) as well as digital droplet PCR (BioRad QX200). The GSR also regularly hosts technology-based seminars and workshops to introduce new technology and provide genomics training to OSUCCC members. In the next funding cycle, the GSR will support the genomics needs of all OSU strategic priorities and Research Programs. Given the robust OSUCCC recruitment, demand for genomics services and new technologies will increase. The GSR will expand its staff, instrumentation, and services before capacity is reached. Plans for the upcoming cycle include purchasing an instrument for long- read sequencing and direct DNA/RNA measurement (e.g., PromethION 24), purchasing an instrument for subcellular spatial transcriptomics (e.g., 10X Genomics Xenium), and optimizing protocols in collaboration with other shared resources for isolation of circulating tumor cells for down-stream genomics interrogation.

title: LARKSPUR-mHealth: A Randomized Controlled Trial of a Remotely Delivered Positive Affect Intervention for Fibromyalgia
text:
Fibromyalgia causes widespread, long-lasting pain and fatigue for millions of Americans, and many treatments
offer limited relief or are hard to access. This study will test LARKSPUR, a fully remote smartphone program
that teaches brief daily skills to build positive emotions—such as gratitude, savoring, and reframing—to help
adults with fibromyalgia reduce pain and improve everyday functioning. If effective, this low-burden approach
could be scaled nationwide, including rural and underserved communities, and reduce pain-related disability
and reliance on pain medicines.

title: Revealing Proteoforms: The Driving Effectors of Biological Function
text:
This project is directed towards the development of powerful new bioanalytical research tools for
identifying and quantifying biological macromolecules. These tools, which will be made widely
available to all researchers, will reveal new information essential to the understanding of both
normal and disease biology, deepening and accelerating the study of human disease
processes.

title: Core C: Biostatistics & Bioinformatics Core
text: The Biostatistics and Bioinformatics Core (BBC) provides state-of-the-art expertise and intellectual resources in biostatistics, bioinformatics, clinical trial design, and statistical computing, which are critical to the success of basic, clinical, translational, and population-based cancer research. The BBC offers cost-effective and efficient solutions for data analysis needs throughout all phases of cancer research, while following NIH data management guidelines. The facility provides U54 investigators from all participating institutions (University of Miami, Emory University, and Morehouse School of Medicine) with biostatistical and bioinformatics assistance for all stages of the three research Projects and Pilot Projects, from design to execution, analysis, interpretation of results, dissemination of findings, and data management and preservation. The BBC also provides education and training to investigators and trainees on novel biostatistical and bioinformatics methodologies relevant to data acquisition and analysis, as well as assistance with manuscript submissions and future grant preparation. To achieve the objectives of the proposed SPORE entitled, PeRsonalized Outreach and Multifaceted Interventions for Screening Enhancement (PROMISE) for Anal and Cervical Cancer Prevention and Treatment, the BBC will work with the Project leaders and Pilot Projects awardees to provide study design and review all laboratory, clinical, and genomic studies including feasibility assessment, power, and sample size analysis for all three primary projects and with investigators from this proposal from the three participating institutions.

title: Administrative and Clinical Trials/Biospecimen Core
text:
The goals of the Administrative and Clinical Trials/Biospecimen Core are to integrate the administrative functions
of all the Projects and Cores and provide infrastructure support. This Core will coordinate the sharing of
biospecimens and data between key collaborators in Spain and the USA and oversee the activities of the P01.

title: Cold-responsive gene and drug delivery-potentiated cryoimmunotherapy
text:
We propose to develop a tumor cell and vasculature-targeted, cold-responsive nanotechnology-potentiated
cryoimmunotherapy for treating both primary and metastatic cancer. This novel cancer therapy strategy may
be invaluable for combating cancer metastasis and recurrence, which are the main causes of mortality in
breast and many other types of cancer, to minimize the mortality and morbidity of cancer patients.

title: Understanding higher-order glycine receptor assemblies in neurotransmission
text:
Neurotransmitter receptors form higher-order clusters at synapses to enable signal
transmission, and the disfunction of which leads to neurological diseases such as
hyperekplexia, chronical neurological pain and reduction in cognitive abilities. Despite their
importance, the physical organization, the functional significance, and whether clustering of
receptors provides additional mechanism of functional regulation is not known. We will use the
state-of-the-art methods and develop novel technologies to characterize receptor assemblies,
first using glycine receptor-gephyrin clusters as an example, and open new research area in
other assemblies ubiquitously found in signal transmission.

title: Biological Aging Across the Life Course: Harmonizing Cohort Biospecimen Archives
text:
Aging blood-based biomarkers (assays: IL-6, TNFa, CRP, GDF15, IGF-1, Cystatin C, NT-proBNP, and hbA1c),
DNA methylation (Illumina EPIC chip), and gene expression (RNA Seq) provide an opportunity to detect aging
related diseases and identify mechanisms linking earlier exposures to later life health. However, little is known
about how these aging biomarkers correlate with each other, the environment, or health over the life course.
This project uses data from three large nationally representative panel studies to examine these associations
over the life course: the Health and Retirement Study (biomarker data for ages 51-110), the National
Longitudinal Study of Adolescent to Adult Health (biomarker data ages 24-42) and the Fragile Families and
Child Wellbeing Study (biomarker data ages 9-22).

title: Concurrent Validity, Test-Retest Reliability, and Sensitivity to Change of Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy for Measuring Language-Related Brain Activity in Post-Stroke Aphasia
text:
Aphasia is a debilitating and often chronic language disorder that has dramatic consequences for
communication and quality of life. Aphasia affects more than 2.5 million Americans, including thousands of
U.S. Veterans. Given evidence that stroke, the leading cause of aphasia, is more common in Veterans than non-
Veterans, VA has a vested interest in developing and implementing novel prognostic and therapeutic tools for
aphasia management. Research on the brain systems implicated in aphasia and its rehabilitation has relied
heavily on fMRI, but fMRI has contraindications that are exclusionary for many people with aphasia. This
project aims to validate functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), a lower-cost, less-restrictive
neuroimaging technology that could reduce barriers to the use of neuroimaging in research and clinical care for
Veterans with aphasia. The project will help establish the viability of fNIRS for studying, predicting, and
potentially accelerating or augmenting aphasia rehabilitation, laying the groundwork for future clinical trials.

title: Regulation of Selenium Metabolism and Selenoprotein Synthesis
text:
Selenium is a nutrient from food that the body needs to make special proteins that protect our cells from damage
and keep our metabolism healthy. This project will study how selenium is absorbed, how it moves through the
body, and how it is used to build these protective proteins. By understanding how selenium works, we aim to
develop new ways to prevent and treat diseases related to cell stress and damage, including heart disease,
diabetes, Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease, thyroid disorders, autoimmune conditions, and cancers.

title: Chemical Probes to Study Formaldehyde Biology
text:
(Public Health Relevance Statement)
Formaldehyde is a major environmental toxin and carcinogen whose aberrant exposure
is connected to diseases spanning liver and cardiovascular disorders, cancer, diabetes,
and neurodegeneration, but at the same time the body continually produces this reactive
carbonyl species during normal physiology. We are developing and applying new chemical
reagents for selective imaging and proteomics of formaldehyde in living systems to identify
its molecular sources and targets, with the long-term goal of understanding how this
reactive small molecule contributes both to normal physiology and disease.

title: Investigating the mechanisms of polycomb group protein mediated fetal hemoglobin silencing
text:
Increasing the expression of fetal hemoglobin is a thoroughly validated therapeutic goal for the
treatment of sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia, which are some of the most common genetic diseases
affecting humans. There is a current unmet need to develop safer, more effective small molecules to increase
fetal hemoglobin expression in patients with these diseases as current gene therapy approaches will remain
out of reach for most patients. This project aims to dissect the role of the polycomb group proteins in fetal
hemoglobin expression with the goal to identify novel targets for fetal hemoglobin reactivation.

title: Clinician cannabis use-related preconceptions perpetuating low quality of prenatal care for women who use cannabis during pregnancy
text: Cannabis is the most commonly used illicit substance during pregnancy, and as legalization and use continue to expand in the United States, it is essential to understand the preconceptions surrounding prenatal cannabis use and their impact on healthcare delivery. Clinician preconceptions about cannabis use have measurable consequences for maternal and infant health outcomes, including reduced prenatal care engagement, higher rates of preterm delivery, low birth weight, and increased maternal morbidity. This study uses natural language processing, reproductive epidemiology, and implementation science to identify how clinician preconceptions manifest in clinical documentation and shape care quality, directly addressing the mechanisms linking clinician behavior to poor pregnancy-related health outcomes.
